why: Replacing the three examples accidentally encouraged earlier, within-unit cuts (especially inside multiword names/titles and before predicates) while removing a clear anti-list-splitting signal; that made many short-span (≤3–10 word) cut positions look better but harmed long-span cohesion and increased harmful splits of lists/predicate frames in larger bins.
lesson: A subsequent revision should preserve training signals that discourage cutting inside multiword names/titles and splitting coordinated/quantifier frames, and avoid examples that implicitly demonstrate or reward preverbal/predicate isolation.
